title: Kirkwood council postpones vote on noise ordinance decibel limits
text:
← Back to the wire
Government
Kirkwood council postpones vote on noise ordinance decibel limits
Council members said they lack an acoustical expert and enforcement guidance before setting firm decibel standards, directing staff to form a subcommittee instead.
The Kirkwood City Council took no vote on a draft noise ordinance Thursday, October 1, during a work session, instead directing staff to continue revising the measure.
City Attorney Sarah presented a redlined draft that added a table offering decibel limits measured either at the receiving property or at the emitting property line, along with proposed changes to nighttime hour restrictions.
ENFORCEMENT CONCERNS A council member said enforcement should be the focus: "I would just ask that then we focus on what's enforceable and that we're putting things in that are enforceable." The same member argued the limit should apply at the receiving property rather than the emitting source, especially near residential areas: "especially when you have business next to residential. You want to enforce the residential, don't we?"
A council member identified as Deb raised concerns about expertise, saying, "I don't think we have an acoustical engineer on staff," and questioned whether a phone-based decibel meter would be legally sufficient, noting the ordinance requires readings from "a properly calibrated decelerator."
Councilman Burquette argued for moving faster to address a specific complaint, saying, "I think we're overkilling this thing personally right now. I think we just need to do something about Billy G's and the sound downtown."
Another council member countered that rushing would be a mistake: "I'm not in favor of rushing this through just to come up with a decibel reading... because there's a lot more to that number that we have yet to really identify."
WHAT HAPPENS NEXT Council members discussed forming a subcommittee or a longer work session with an outside expert to study the issue further. Darren, a staff member, said he would email his list of recommended changes to begin that process.
